SearchQueryParam.name: q
SearchQueryParam.description:
Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by
spaces are ANDed together.

**URL Encoding:** This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP.
Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation
show human-readable syntax for clarity.

## Syntax

| Pattern | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `term` | Full-text exact match | `john` |
| `*term*` | Full-text contains | `*john*` |
| `term*` | Full-text starts with | `john*` |
| `*term` | Full-text ends with | `*smith` |
| `field:value` | Exact match on field | `status:approved` |
| `field:*value*` | Contains (case-insensitive) | `name:*john*` |
| `field:value*` | Starts with | `name:john*` |
| `field:*value` | Ends with | `email:*@example.com` |
| `field:"value"` | Quoted value (for spaces) | `name:"john doe"` |
| `field.nested:value` | Nested field (dot notation) | `address.state:CA` |
| `field:>value` | Greater than | `income:>1000` |
| `field:>=value` | Greater than or equal | `income:>=1000` |
| `field:<value` | Less than | `income:<5000` |
| `field:<=value` | Less than or equal | `income:<=5000` |
| `field:val1,val2` | Match any value (OR) | `status:approved,pending` |
| `-field:value` | Exclude / negate | `-status:denied` |
| `field:*` | Field exists (not null) | `email:*` |
| `-field:*` | Field does not exist | `-deletedAt:*` |

## Examples

- `john` — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
- `*john*` — contains "john" in searchable fields
- `name:*smith*` — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
- `email:*@example.com` — email ends with "@example.com"
- `status:approved` — exact match on status field
- `status:approved,pending` — status is "approved" OR "pending"
- `income:>=1000` — income greater than or equal to 1000
- `created:>2024-01-01` — created after January 1, 2024
- `status:approved income:>=1000` — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
- `-status:denied` — exclude records with status "denied"
- `-deletedAt:*` — only records where deletedAt does not exist
- `applicant.state:CA` — nested field filter

## URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

| Character | Encoded |
|-----------|---------|
| (space) | `%20` or `+` |
| `"` | `%22` |
| `:` | `%3A` |
| `>` | `%3E` |
| `<` | `%3C` |
| `,` | `%2C` |

**Example:**
```
Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000
URL-encoded:    q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000
```

SortParam.name: sort
SortParam.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field
with `-` for descending order. The first field is the primary sort;
subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

**URL Encoding:** This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP.
Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples below show
human-readable syntax for clarity.

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's
`x-sortable.fields` extension. Sending a field name not present in that
list returns `400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE`. Sending a field name that doesn't
exist on the resource schema returns `400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD`. When this
parameter is omitted, the operation's `x-sortable.default` (if declared)
is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured
tie-breaker (default `id`) is always appended for stable pagination.

See `api-patterns.yaml#sorting` for the full convention and
`docs/architecture/x-extensions.md` for the extension shape.

## Syntax

| Pattern | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `fieldName` | Ascending | `sort=createdAt` |
| `-fieldName` | Descending | `sort=-createdAt` |
| `field1,field2` | Multi-field | `sort=status,-priority` |
| `nested.field` | Nested field via dot notation | `sort=name.lastName` |

## Examples

- `sort=createdAt` — oldest first
- `sort=-createdAt` — newest first
- `sort=-priority,dueDate` — highest priority first, then oldest due date
- `sort=name.lastName,name.firstName` — alphabetical by surname, then given name

IdempotencyKeyParam.name: Idempotency-Key

A key the client makes for one create, so a retry is not a second create.
Send the same key with every retry of the same request: the first is
created, and a repeat gets the same response back. The same key with a
different request is refused with 422. Keys are scoped to the caller.

Any value unique to the operation works; a UUID is recommended. An
operation that lists this parameter requires it. Follows the IETF HTTP API
working group's `Idempotency-Key` header draft, and the convention Stripe
and others use.

info.title: Transcripts
info.description:
The written record of a conversation. Starting a transcript opens it for
recording; pausing takes the conversation off the record; closing ends it.
A transcript refers to what it records — an interview, a call — and names
the profile it was started under, which says the transcription service,
and the client and model that produced its lines. Updating corrects what
it records; deleting removes it, and the event left behind says which one
and by whom.

A profile is a state's choice of transcription service and languages for
a kind of conversation. The deployment's config seeds them; they can be
added and changed here, never deleted, so every transcript's profile
still exists.

Its entries are its timeline, in the order things happened: lines, gaps
where nothing was captured, and pauses. Every time on a transcript and its
entries is the client's — when it started, paused, resumed and closed, and
when each line was said — so they are compared on one clock.

interviewPrompts.hasUnemployedWorkEligib.interviewPromptRationale: Identifies household members aged 16–59 who are not employed and have not yet been screened for general work requirement exemptions.

interviewPrompts.hasStudentMembers.interviewPromptRationale: Identifies household members enrolled at least half-time in higher education who are subject to student eligibility restrictions.

interviewPrompts.hasNonCitizenMembers.interviewPromptRationale: Identifies non-citizen household members who must be screened for qualified alien status and sponsor income deeming rules.

interviewPrompts.incomeInconsistencyProm.interviewPromptRationale: Probe for undisclosed income sources or assistance when monthly income is less than monthly expenses.
interviewQuestions: Your application shows monthly income of [income] and monthly expenses of [expenses]. Can you tell me about any other income sources or assistance your household receives?
Does anyone in the household receive help with expenses from family, friends, or community organizations?

interviewPrompts.workRequirementPrompt.interviewPromptRationale: Screen non-employed household members aged 16–59 for general work requirement exemptions before determining work registration obligations.
interviewQuestions: Is [member] currently able to work — are there any physical or mental health conditions that limit their ability to work?
Is [member] currently caring for a child under 6 or an incapacitated person in the household?
Is [member] currently enrolled in school, job training, or a work program through another benefit program?
Is [member] currently working at least 30 hours per week or earning the federal minimum wage equivalent?

interviewPrompts.studentEligibilityPromp.interviewPromptRationale: Screen higher-education students for SNAP eligibility exceptions — most students enrolled at least half-time are ineligible unless they meet one of the statutory exceptions.
interviewQuestions: Is [member] currently working at least 20 hours per week?
Is [member] participating in a state or federally-funded work-study program?
Is [member] enrolled in a school-sponsored job training or vocational program?
Is [member] caring for a dependent child under 6, or a child aged 6–11 when adequate childcare is unavailable?
Is [member] receiving TANF assistance?
Is [member] a single parent enrolled full-time with a dependent child under 12?

interviewPrompts.immigrationStatusPrompt.interviewPromptRationale: Determine qualified alien status and apply sponsor income and resource deeming rules for non-citizen household members.
interviewQuestions: What is [member]'s current immigration status?
When did [member] enter the United States?
Does [member] have a sponsor who signed an I-864 Affidavit of Support on or after December 19, 1997?
If yes — what is the sponsor's current income and resources?

interviewPrompts.changeVerificationPromp.interviewPromptRationale: Identify and document all changes in household circumstances that occurred between the application date and the interview date, and determine what verification is required.
interviewQuestions: Since you submitted your application, have there been any changes to who lives in your household?
Have there been any changes to income — new jobs, job losses, raises, or changes to other income sources?
Have there been any changes to your household's expenses — rent, utilities, childcare, or medical costs?
Have there been any other changes in your household's situation we should know about?

oneof-discriminator.description: Inline oneOf with a discriminator property, where all variants are defined within the same file (not via external $ref). Exercises discriminated union rendering, discriminator label resolution, and variant expansion in the explorer.

anyof.description: anyOf composition — a field that may satisfy more than one schema simultaneously (e.g., a record with both electronic and manual verification on file). Exercises anyOf rendering and the semantic distinction from oneOf.

additional-properties-map.description: Map type using additionalProperties to allow arbitrary key-value pairs (e.g., labels or metadata). Exercises additionalProperties rendering in the explorer and map validation in the schema validator.

read-only-field.description: Field marked readOnly: true — server-generated and never accepted in write operations. Common for IDs, computed values, and lifecycle timestamps. Exercises readOnly rendering in the explorer and write-operation filtering.

deprecated-field.description: Field marked deprecated: true with a migration note pointing to its replacement. Exercises deprecated field rendering in the explorer and tooling warnings.

string-format.description: String field with a format constraint (uuid, date-time, date, email, etc.). Exercises format rendering in the explorer and format validation.

polymorphic-base.description: Base schema extended via allOf in Create and Update variants. The Create variant adds required fields; the Update variant applies minProperties: 1 for partial updates. Exercises allOf merging and the Create/Update schema pattern.

array-of-enum.description: Array of enum values. Exercises array-of-enum rendering in the explorer and array item validation in the schema validator.

x-enum-source.description: Enum values resolved at build time from an external source (e.g., a state machine's state IDs) via the x-enum-source extension, rather than hardcoded in the OpenAPI spec. Exercises the resolver's x-enum-source injection.

nullable-state-gated-field.description: Nullable field that is only present after a lifecycle transition (e.g., a timestamp set when an application is submitted). Exercises nullable field rendering and the pattern of state-gated fields.

nullable-conditional-field.description: Nullable field whose presence depends on another field's value (e.g., a benefit amount present only when eligible is true). Exercises nullable field handling and conditional presence patterns.

external-ref-shared-defs.description: External $ref to a shared $defs schema in a separate file. Exercises the resolver's cross-file $ref resolution and the explorer's external schema name rendering.

external-ref-defs-oneof.description: External $ref to a $defs schema that is itself a oneOf with a discriminator. Exercises: (1) cross-file $ref resolution, (2) discriminated union rendering with labeled variants, (3) field inventory handling of oneOf inside an external $defs ref.

allof-inline-required.description: allOf composition that adds inline required fields without duplicating properties (e.g., a Create variant that adds a required field to a base schema). Exercises the resolver's allOf merging and the explorer's allOf rendering.

paginated-list.description: Collection endpoint returning items/total/limit/offset/hasNext. The standard blueprint pagination envelope. Exercises paginated list rendering and parameter validation (limit, offset, sort, search).

sub-resource.description: Resource nested under a parent at a path like /parents/{id}/children. Full CRUD scoped to the parent. Exercises nested routing, parent FK validation, and sub-resource list/detail rendering in the explorer.

singleton-sub-resource.description: Single resource nested under a parent at a path like /parents/{id}/summary, with no item-level ID. Accessed only through the parent. Exercises singleton sub-resource routing and composition rendering.

intra-domain-fk.description: Intra-domain x-relationship foreign key linking a sub-resource back to its parent resource within the same domain. Exercises cross-reference rendering in the explorer and FK validation.

cross-domain-fk.description: Cross-domain x-relationship foreign key linking a resource in one domain to a resource in another. Exercises cross-domain reference rendering and FK validation across domain boundaries.

rpc-state-machine-action.description: RPC-style state machine action with a generated POST endpoint. Exercises the RPC overlay generator, x-relationship tagging, and state machine → API cross-linking in the explorer.

state-machine-guard.description: Named boolean condition (CEL expression) attached to a state machine action. The action can only be triggered when all guard conditions pass. Exercises guard evaluation, actor role checking, and guard composition (any/all).

state-machine-timer.description: Timer declaration on a state machine. The scheduling service emits a callback event ({domain}.{id}) when the timer fires; the machine subscribes to react. Exercises timer declaration rendering and the timer → event subscription link.

state-machine-subscription.description: State machine subscribing to a domain event emitted by a different domain. The handler runs steps (create, emit, call) automatically when the event arrives. Exercises cross-domain event subscription and handler rendering.

state-machine-event.description: Domain event emitted on a state machine transition. Exercises AsyncAPI event catalog generation and event → state machine cross-linking.

cross-domain-event.description: Domain event consumed by downstream domains outside the emitting domain. Exercises event catalog cross-domain consumer rendering.

composition.description: Read-only singleton resource assembled from fields across multiple resources, generated from a compositions contract. Produces a GET endpoint nested under the parent resource (e.g. /applications/{id}/summary). Exercises the composition generator, x-relationship injection, and singleton rendering in the explorer.

overlay.description: Field or element added or modified by an adopter overlay. Overlays add state-required fields, tighten enums, and set global configuration (x-casing, x-pagination, x-search, x-relationship, x-event-type-prefix). Exercises the overlay resolver and adopter-level customization patterns.

ruleset-output-fact.description: Output fact from a ruleset — a fact declared in the outputs list and returned by the REST endpoint. Exercises the rules engine → API endpoint link in the explorer (Rules badge).

ruleset-intermediate-fact.description: Intermediate fact used internally by other facts but not returned by the REST endpoint. Exercises fact graph dependency rendering in the rules-docs visualizer.

array-of-oneof.description: Array whose items are a oneOf discriminated union (e.g., EvaluationResult returning EvaluationFact variants). Exercises array-of-oneOf rendering, discriminator label resolution, and schema variant expansion.

snap-application-acceptance.description: SNAP application acceptance requirements — agencies must accept applications on the day of initial contact and must not discourage or delay submission.

snap-right-to-apply.description: SNAP right-to-apply — any household wishing to participate must be allowed to file an application, and the filing date establishes the benefit month.

snap-processing-clock.description: SNAP application processing standards — 30-day processing clock from date of filing; expedited service within 7 days for qualifying households.

medicaid-processing-clock.description: Medicaid application processing standards — 45-day processing clock for most applicants; 90 days for disability-based applicants.

snap-notice-of-action.description: SNAP notice of adverse action — agencies must provide timely and adequate written notice before reducing, suspending, or terminating benefits.

snap-notice-of-eligibility.description: SNAP notice of eligibility determination — written notice of approval or denial with reason, rights, and certification period.

medicaid-notice-of-eligibility.description: Medicaid notice of eligibility determination — written notice of approval or denial with reason, appeal rights, and effective date.

snap-fair-hearing-rights.description: SNAP fair hearing rights — households have the right to request a fair hearing within 90 days of any adverse action notice.

snap-interview-toolkit.description: FNS SNAP Interview Toolkit — six essential interview functions, probe triggers for inconsistency flags, verification requirements, and interview conclusion standards.

snap-general-work-requirement.description: SNAP general work requirements — able-bodied adults aged 16–59 must register for work, accept suitable employment, and participate in assigned employment and training programs. Exemptions include physical/mental incapacity, caregiving, school enrollment, and participation in other programs.

snap-abawd-work-requirement.description: SNAP able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) work requirement — individuals aged 18–54 without dependents are limited to 3 months of benefits in any 36-month period unless they meet work, exemption, or waiver criteria.

snap-student-eligibility.description: SNAP eligibility rules for students enrolled at least half-time in higher education — generally ineligible unless they meet one of the statutory exceptions (employment, work-study, dependent care, TANF participation, etc.).

snap-expedited-processing.description: SNAP expedited service — households with gross monthly income below $150 and liquid resources below $100 (or migrant/seasonal farmworkers) must receive benefits within 7 days of application.

snap-expedited-screening.description: SNAP expedited screening criteria — agencies must screen all applications on the day of receipt and identify households entitled to expedited service.

qualified-alien-eligibility.description: SNAP eligibility for non-citizens — only qualified aliens are eligible; status categories include LPRs, refugees, asylees, and other federally defined categories with varying waiting periods.

prwora-sponsor-deeming.description: PRWORA sponsor income deeming — income and resources of a sponsor who signed an I-864 Affidavit of Support on or after December 19, 1997 are deemed available to the sponsored non-citizen for SNAP purposes.

snap-household-composition.description: SNAP household composition rules — defines who must be included in a SNAP household, including mandatory household members, separate household rules, and treatment of boarders, roommates, and institutionalized individuals.

snap-income-verification.description: SNAP income verification requirements — agencies must verify earned and unearned income at application and recertification, including acceptable documentary evidence and collateral contact standards.

snap-elderly-disabled-deductions.description: SNAP deductions for elderly and disabled households — households with an elderly or disabled member may claim excess medical expense deductions and are exempt from the gross income test.

snap-benefit-calculation.description: SNAP benefit calculation — net monthly income is used to determine benefit allotment; benefit equals 30% of net income subtracted from the maximum allotment for household size.

chip-age-eligibility.description: CHIP age eligibility — states must define an upper age limit for CHIP eligibility (up to age 19), and may extend coverage to unborn children and former foster youth up to age 26 under state plan options.

medicaid-caretaker-relative.description: Medicaid caretaker relative eligibility — states must provide Medicaid to caretaker relatives of dependent children who meet income and resource standards, including parents and other adults who are the primary caregiver.

medicaid-cost-sharing.description: Medicaid cost sharing — limits on premiums, copayments, and other cost sharing for Medicaid enrollees, including aggregate limits by income level and prohibition on cost sharing for certain populations and services.

medicaid-determination-documentation.description: Medicaid eligibility verification — agencies must verify eligibility factors through electronic data sources before requesting documentation from applicants; paper documentation may be requested only when electronic verification is unavailable.

procedures.description: Request a time-based callback from the scheduling service. Pass fireAfter (a duration) or fireAt (an absolute timestamp), and a callback naming the event to publish when it elapses. Nothing here waits: the request is an event, and whatever provides scheduling answers it — in a deployment a scheduler, in a test a mock stub, which is what makes a 72-hour deadline testable in a second.

info.title: Scheduling Domain Events
info.description:
The timer request channel, which is the whole scheduling surface this
fixture needs. A domain asks for a time-based callback by publishing
`scheduling.timer.requested` with the event to fire when it elapses;
whatever provides scheduling answers it. Nothing in this contract set
implements a scheduler, which is the point — the mock server's timer stub
stands in, so a deadline measured in days is exercised in a second.

TimerRequestedMessage.name: scheduling.timer.requested
TimerRequestedMessage.summary: Emitted by the platform requestTimer procedure. A scheduler registers the timer and publishes the callback event on expiry.

info.title: The application walk-through
info.description:
A household applies for SNAP online and a caseworker takes the application from submission to close, showing what the mock does from the contracts alone:

- separate shapes for what a client writes and what the system keeps, and derived fields
- a file upload and an expanded relationship
- search, sorting and paging
- a lifecycle that refuses moves made out of turn
- a composed view, and rules that explain their answers
- one event log across every domain
- the mock's own stand-ins and reset

workflows.summary: An application from creation to close, through every kind of thing the contracts declare.

steps.description:
Create an application

- You sent an `ApplicationCreate` and got back an `Application` — two schemas, not one. The contract declares the shape a client may write separately from the shape the system keeps.
- `id`, `confirmationNumber`, `status`, `submittedAt`, `openedAt` are marked `readOnly`, so they are not on the shape you sent at all. The server filled them in because the contract says they exist.
- `programCount` is declared as a derived field, with the expression `this.programsAppliedFor.size()`. Nothing stores it: the mock evaluates that expression every time the record is read.
- `channel` is an enum in the contract — `online`, `phone`, `in_person`, `mail`. A value outside that list is refused by the schema, and no validation was written for this endpoint to do it.
- `201` and `400`, `422`, `500` are all declared on this operation, and the mock worked out which one applied and returned it. None of them are canned.

Upload a document

- This body is `multipart/form-data`, not JSON. The contract declares `file` with `format: binary`, which is how an OpenAPI document says bytes, and `documentTypeId`, `title` alongside it as ordinary fields. One operation in the whole set sends something that is not JSON, and it is the one most mocks fall over on.
- What came back describes the upload and does not contain it. The bytes were hashed as they were read and then dropped — `contentHash` and `sizeBytes` are kept on the version this created, which `latestVersionId` names, and the file itself is nowhere. Nothing the mock holds can leak something nobody meant to share.

file.content: Hashed on the way in, and then thrown away.

steps.description:
Edit and attach the document

- A third shape: `ApplicationUpdate` is what you may send here, and it is not `Application` either.
- `proofOfIncomeDocumentId` is the id of the `Document` you uploaded a moment ago, and `proofOfIncomeDocument` is the whole record. The document-management domain declares that shape, this one declares a relationship to it, and the mock put what the id points at where the id was — one request rather than two, and nothing joining them in a client.
- `updatedAt` moved on its own. Everything the request did not mention is as it was.
- `id`, `confirmationNumber`, `status` are not on `ApplicationUpdate` at all, so there is no way to send them and nothing to reject.
- `200` and `400`, `404`, `422`, `500` are all declared on this operation, and the mock worked out which one applied and returned it. None of them are canned.

List the applications

- `q`, `sort`, `limit` are in the request above, and `q`, `limit`, `offset`, `sort`, `status`, `channel` are all declared on the operation. Declaring them was the whole of the work — the searching, filtering and paging came with them.
- `x-sortable` lists `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `submittedAt`, `status`, `channel` as the fields that may be sorted, and `-createdAt` as the order when a request does not say. Any other field is refused by name. The allowlist is that declaration — there is no check written for this endpoint.
- `items`, `total`, `limit`, `offset` — the page envelope is the contract's shape, not a convention the mock chose.

Stand in for the scheduler

- Nothing in the contract set implements a scheduler, and `submit` asks for one `72 hours` out. That gap is declared, not accidental.
- This registers a stand-in for `scheduling.timer.requested`, so the callback lands the moment it is asked for. The contract did not change — the thing on the other end of it did.

Submit the application

- The contract declares this move as `draft → submitted`. From any other state the mock refuses it — not from a check somebody wrote for this endpoint, but by reading that line.
- This action also calls `requestTimer` with a `fireAfter` of 72 hours, which emits `scheduling.timer.requested`. The stand-in you registered answers it immediately, so `intake.review_reminder` is already in the event log rather than three days away.
- `slaTypeCode` and `slaInfo` are filled from an SLA contract: `snap_standard` runs 30 days, warns at 80% of it, and stops while `status` is `withdrawn`. The clock is a declaration, not a cron job somebody remembered to write.
- `submittedAt` is annotated with `snap-processing-clock`, which the shared policy registry resolves to 7 CFR § 273.2(g). SNAP application processing standards — 30-day processing clock from date of filing; expedited service within 7 days for qualifying households.
- `200` and `400`, `404`, `409`, `500` are all declared on this operation, and the mock worked out which one applied and returned it. A `409` is declared here because the contract anticipates this call being made out of turn.

Close it from the wrong state

- The contract declares this move as `under_review → closed`, and the record is not in that state yet. Nothing checked for this case on purpose — the mock reads that line and answers from it, the same line the moves that worked read.
- Every lifecycle in the set is enforced this way, so a state machine nobody implemented is still a state machine you cannot get around.

Open the application

- `openedAt` was null until now. The lifecycle declares `set: openedAt = $now` on this move, so the field is written because the state machine says so — there is no handler here that writes it.

Close the application

- This move emits `intake.application.closed`, which the log a few steps on will have in it. Nothing subscribed to it and nothing called a publisher: the action declares an `emit` and the mock does it.

Build a view of the application

- Nothing stores this shape. The composition names `programsAppliedFor`, `status` and the mock reads those fields off the stored application when you ask for it.
- It also pulls in `members`, which live in their own collection. Reading this without the composition means a request for the application and 1 more for the rest, then assembling them in the client.
- This is where the `_links` on the application came from. `applicationSummary`, `applicationReview` set `parentLink`, so the mock added `/summary`, `/review` to every application it returns. The application's own schema says nothing about either of them.

Evaluate expeditedSnap

- The answer is not one expression but a chain of named facts. The last is `isExpeditedEligible = (isLowIncome && hasLowResources) || isCombinedUnderShelter || isMigrantWithLowResources` — so the system can say which condition carried, not just what it concluded.
- `incomeThreshold` is an input with a default of `150`, citing 7 CFR § 273.2(i)(1)(i). It is a number Congress changes, so the contract treats it as one rather than burying it in code.
- `resourceThreshold` is an input with a default of `100`, citing 7 CFR § 273.2(i)(1)(i). It is a number Congress changes, so the contract treats it as one rather than burying it in code.
- Every fact comes back as a `state` and a `value` rather than a bare answer. `complete` means everything it needed was given to it; a fact that fell back to a declared default says `placeholder` instead, so a caller can tell a real conclusion from a provisional one.

Evaluate interviewPrompts

- The answer is not one expression but a chain of named facts. The last is `changeVerificationPrompt = application.hasChangedCircumstances` — so the system can say which condition carried, not just what it concluded.
- `interviewPrompts.incomeInconsistencyPrompt` carries more than a true or false. The annotations attach `snap-interview-toolkit` to it and 2 interview questions to go with it, so the rule that raises a prompt and the words somebody says out loud are one declaration rather than two that drift apart.

See what the walk emitted

- Every change you made emitted one of these, and nothing asked for them. Uploading a document wrote to this log; so did submitting, opening and closing.
- The types are declared as channels in the contract set — `transcription.transcript.created`, `transcription.transcript.updated`, `transcription.transcript.deleted`, `transcription.transcript_entry.created`, and the rest.
- One log, every domain. Nothing wired them together.

Narrow the log to one record

- `q` is full text over the whole log, narrowed here to the application you created. The document upload drops out — it happened, but to a different subject.
- What is left was written by more than one domain. Submitting the application is what made eligibility start a determination, and neither domain was wired to the other: each declares its own channel, and this log is all they share.
- `sort` works here for the same reason it worked on the applications — this operation declares its own `x-sortable`, over `time`, `type`, `source`. Nothing was written twice to make both endpoints sortable.

Empty the store

- No contract declares this endpoint. It belongs to the mock, not to the system it is running.
- It clears records, never contracts — afterwards the API is exactly the API it was.

Put the data back

- The records come from the contract set's own `*-mock-data.yaml`, and are checked against the same schemas as anything you send.

info.title: A transcript, from start to close
info.description:
A caseworker's interview software transcribes an interview from start to close, then abandons a second transcript, exercising the transcription domain end to end:

- profiles, and what a transcript needs before it can start
- a timeline of lines, gaps and pauses, each judged by when it started
- retries recognized by their Idempotency-Key, and entries that never change
- closing, and the idle timeout, with the mock standing in for the scheduler

workflows.summary: Start, record, pause, resume and close a transcript, and see what it refuses.

steps.description:
Add a profile

- An administrator adds the profile English interviews run under: the transcription service and its languages.
- Profiles the config seeds are marked `source: system`; one added here is `user`.

Start without a model

- Refused with 409: under a profile with a transcription service, a transcript says which model produced its lines.
- The refusal names the condition not met, from the guard's description.

Start under a profile that does not exist

- The profile id doesn't belong to any profile, so the transcript is refused with 409.

Start the transcript

- The caseworker's software starts a transcript of the interview, under the profile.
- It begins in `recording`, with `startedAt` by the software's clock.

Add the first line

- A finished line arrives, with an `Idempotency-Key`.
- Its start and end times come from the transcription software's clock, not the server's, so every time on a transcript is compared on one clock.

payload.text: Can you tell me who lives with you?
payload.speaker: staff

steps.description:
Send it again

- The connection drops before the answer comes back, so the software sends the line again with the same key.
- It gets the same line back, marked `Idempotent-Replayed`, not a second one.

payload.text: Can you tell me who lives with you?
payload.speaker: staff

steps.description:
Go off the record

- The applicant asks to stop. Pausing adds an open pause entry to the timeline.

A line said just before the pause

- It arrives just after the pause began, but it started on the record, so it is kept.
- A line is judged by when it started, not when it arrived.

payload.text: My two kids and my mother.
payload.speaker: client

steps.description:
A line said during the pause

- Refused with 409: nothing said off the record is kept, even from faulty software.

A lost stretch overlapping the pause

- Refused with 409: the pause already accounts for that time.

Back on the record

- Resuming gives the open pause its end time.

A late line from inside the past pause

- Still refused: the pause has ended, but the line started inside it.

Read the timeline

- Lines, gaps and pauses in the order they happened, by `startedAt`.
- The pause is in it, with its end time.

Try to change an entry

- Refused with 403: entries do not change, and only the system may update one.

Close the transcript

- The interview ends.
- `lastActivityAt` says when the software was last heard from: the end of its last line.

A line after the close

- Refused with 409: nothing is added after the close.

Add a profile with an idle timeout

- Its transcripts close themselves after 30 quiet minutes: `idleTimeout: PT30M`.

Stand in for the scheduler

- Nobody waits 30 minutes in a test. A stub on the mock answers the next idle check request at once, as if the time had passed.
- This step calls the mock's own route, so the scenario runs against the mock.

Start a transcript and go quiet

- The software starts a transcript and is never heard from again.

It closed itself

- The idle check found nothing since it was asked for, so the transcript closed.
- It closed at the time it was last heard from: here, when it started.
